sections.html:
Huntsville is Alabama's largest city and the seat of Madison County, in the Appalachian part of north Alabama just south of the Tennessee line. Annexation has pushed its borders into Limestone, Morgan and Marshall Counties as well, making it the only Alabama city that sits in four counties. The 2025 population is put at 233,627, up 8.7 percent from 215,006 in 2020.

The city covers 225.2 square miles, with its farthest points about 32 miles apart, at an elevation near 577 feet. Because of that spread, check the county on your deed. Madison County holds most Huntsville parcels, but a house in an annexed western or southern pocket can belong to another county for tax and recording purposes.

Historic districts include Twickenham, Old Town and the Lowe Mill area, with homes dating from the early 1800s to the early 1900s. Owners of houses like these often deal with older plumbing, wiring and rooflines when they sell. Population jumped from 16,437 in 1950 to 72,365 in 1960, so a large share of the remaining housing dates from the postwar boom.

sections.h2: Why newcomers and sellers move quickly
sections.html: Aerospace and military technology run the local economy, around Redstone Arsenal, Cummings Research Park, NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center and the Jetplex industrial park. Large projects bring new residents, and relocation is one reason people sell on short timelines. Some owners also inherit a Huntsville home while living out of state and want a simple exit.

sections.h2: Storms, rain and the ground under the house
sections.html:
Huntsville gets more than 54 inches of rain a year, with the heaviest months from November to May and December the wettest. Thunderstorms bring large hail, damaging straight-line winds and tornadoes, and the city lies in Dixie Alley, a region prone to long-track tornadoes. On April 27, 2011, an EF5 tornado near Browns Ferry caused a multi-day power outage across north Alabama, and nine people were killed in Madison County.

Roofs and siding take the brunt, and owners who have lived through storms often sell with patches or older shingles still in place. The ground is karst, with limestone bedrock and caves below, so an inspector working for a buyer will check drainage and the foundation closely. Lots on the slopes of Monte Sano, Wade Mountain and Rainbow Mountain shed water differently than flat ground in the valley.

Huntsville City Schools serves most of the city. The part in Morgan County falls in the Morgan County School District, and a few parcels belong to the Madison County and Limestone County districts. Be ready to tell buyers which district your address is in.

Land added over the years includes about 21.5 square miles west into Limestone County in the early 2000s, 1.03 square miles in Morgan County in 2018 and more than 1,000 acres in Marshall County in 2025. A house in one of those pockets uses the tax collector and probate office of its own county.

Property tax on Huntsville parcels in Madison County is billed by the county tax collector. Payment is due October 1 and late after December 31. Nothing in state law requires a bill to be mailed before that, though the office sends a courtesy notice by October 1.

Inside the city limits the county rate is $5.80 per $100 of assessed value, with the regular homestead deduction applied afterward. After December 31 a $5 late fee applies, plus interest of 1 percent per month. A tax lien sale and auction is held online each May.

Bills follow the owner of record on October 1 of the prior year, so one can still reach you after you sell. Ask the closing office to prorate it.

sections.h2: Preparing a Huntsville house for sale
sections.html:
Storm-weathered roofs and older systems are the usual weak points, so list them honestly. If you know of past water in a crawl space, drainage trouble on a hillside lot or foundation cracking, tell the buyer. Karst ground makes inspectors careful, and a seller who raised the issue first looks better than one who was caught.

If you are selling an older house in a historic area, ask the city about any review that applies to exterior work before you promise a buyer changes. For a newer house, gather the plat and any permits for additions or a finished garage.

sections.h2: Questions buyers ask about a Huntsville house
sections.html:
• Which county holds the parcel, and which school district serves it?
  • How old is the roof, and has hail or wind ever damaged it?
  • Is the lot on a hillside, and does water drain away from the foundation?
  • Is the tax bill current, and what does the homestead deduction cover?
  • Are there tenants, and when does the lease end?

Answer these in your first message and a buyer can decide faster, which matters when your timeline is short.

The probate office that takes Madison County deeds sits in the Madison County Service Center, 1918 Memorial Parkway NW. The county tells new owners to verify the recording, then assess the property with the tax assessor and claim exemptions.

The state recording tax of 50 cents per $500 of value comes from Alabama Code 40-22-1, and proof of the real price must be attached. Payment comes before the clerk accepts the deed.

sections.h2: Selling with tenants or an inherited house
sections.html: A rented house can be sold with the lease in place, so read its terms and give any notices it requires. With an inherited house that owes taxes, the balance is paid from the proceeds at closing, and court papers must show who may sign.

After you accept an offer, a title search looks for liens, unpaid taxes and ownership gaps. If a mortgage is open, the lender sends a payoff figure. On closing day you sign the deed and settlement statement, the payoff and tax split are handled, and the deed goes to the probate office of the county where the parcel lies.

Bring a photo ID and every key and garage opener. If heirs share the title, all of them sign. If you live out of state, ask whether the closing can be handled by mail or at a title office near you.

Cash buyers close without a mortgage lender, so no loan appraisal can derail the sale. In a fast-growing city that appeals to owners who want certainty about timing.

  • Inherited homes with unpaid taxes.
  • Rental properties with tenants in place.
  • Houses with storm damage or old roofs.
  • Owners moving for a job at Redstone or a plant.

A title search and any taxes owed still come first, as in every sale.

faqs.q: What is the population of Huntsville, AL?
faqs.a: About 233,627 as of July 1, 2025, up from 215,006 at the 2020 census.
Madison, Limestone, Morgan and Marshall Counties. Madison County holds most of the city and is the county seat.

faqs.q: When are Madison County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Due October 1, delinquent after December 31, when a $5 late fee and 1 percent monthly interest begin.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Huntsville?
faqs.a: At the Madison County probate office in the Madison County Service Center at 1918 Memorial Parkway NW, for parcels in Madison County.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Huntsville house with tenants in it?
faqs.a: Yes. The house can be sold subject to the lease. Read the terms and give any required notices.
